node-1.label: After acupuncture treatment, the patient experienced persistent chest pain while breathing, shortness of breath, and difficulty walking even 20 steps.

node-2.label: 26-year-old male visited Korean Medicine Hospital for acute indigestion; initially presented with acute indigestion, tenderness, and pain in the midback after having lunch.

node-3.label: Social history includes smoking 0.1 box/day and alcohol consumption 1 time/month, 2 bottles of soju.

why.why: Radiologist analysis of the retrieved imaging shows CT evidence of air and blood in the chest cavity and pulmonary hemorrhage, establishing hemopneumothorax. This directly confirms the intrathoracic pathology and, together with recent acupuncture, pleuritic chest pain, dyspnea, and exertional intolerance, makes acupuncture pneumothorax the leading diagnosis. Confidence is raised from 0.85 to 0.95.

The new CT evidence of hemopneumothorax and pulmonary hemorrhage fully accounts for the pleuritic chest pain, dyspnea, and difficulty walking. The smoking and alcohol history is nonspecific, and the close temporal relationship to acupuncture argues against a cardiopulmonary ischemic event; confidence is therefore lowered to 0.02.

Imaging-documented hemopneumothorax and pulmonary hemorrhage provide a definitive intrathoracic explanation for the dyspnea and exertional intolerance, so musculoskeletal/GI pain cannot explain the main symptoms. The midback tenderness is better explained by referred pain from pleural/diaphragmatic irritation; confidence is lowered to 0.01.

node-8.label: Chest CT reveals air and blood in the right chest cavity with pulmonary hemorrhage

why.why: Radiologist analysis confirms that CT evidence of air and blood in the right chest cavity with pulmonary hemorrhage establishes hemopneumothorax, and the immediate temporal relationship with recent acupuncture strongly supports acupuncture-induced pneumothorax as the leading diagnosis with high confidence. This expert confirmation, combined with the existing evidence of pleuritic chest pain, dyspnea, and exertional intolerance immediately after acupuncture, directly strengthens the causal attribution of the hemopneumothorax to acupuncture. Confidence is therefore raised from 0.90 to 0.95; the lack of quantitative details such as pneumothorax size and needle track leaves only minor residual uncertainty about the exact puncture path.
